r.정치 구도: A parliamentary system led by a prime minister, with a single-chamber parliament. The president is elected by parliament and has limited real power. Fidesz, in power for 16 years from 2010, used its two-thirds majority to write a new constitution and was criticized for reshaping the electoral system, courts and media in its own favor. In the April 2026 election Tisza, an opposition party that grew rapidly from 2024, won more than two-thirds of the seats and took power. The new government has cancelled the withdrawal from the International Criminal Court and applied to join the European Public Prosecutor's Office, working to repair ties with the EU. How fast and how far to dismantle the institutions built by the previous government is now the central political question.

t.why: It joined NATO in 1999 and the EU in 2004. The previous government stayed close to Russia and repeatedly threatened vetoes over aid to Ukraine and sanctions on Russia, delaying EU decisions that require unanimity. It imports much of its oil and gas from Russia by pipeline, and a Russian company is building the expansion of its nuclear plant, so energy and foreign policy are tied together. The EU froze funds over rule-of-law and corruption concerns, then in 2026 agreed with the new government to release them in return for reforms. The 1920 Treaty of Trianon cost Hungary two-thirds of its territory, leaving large Hungarian communities in Romania, Slovakia, Serbia, Ukraine and elsewhere, an issue that always hangs over relations with its neighbors.
t.rel: Long friendly toward Russia, it clashed often with the EU. Repairing relations is the task after the 2026 change of government, and Hungarian minorities in neighboring countries are a constant diplomatic issue.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations were established on February 1, 1989, making Hungary the first country in the former Eastern Bloc to recognize South Korea, followed by the Soviet Union and China. In 2017 Samsung SDI decided to build an EV battery plant in Göd, and SK On has built plants too, making Hungary a key European base for Korean battery makers. Korea sells fine chemical materials for batteries and machinery, and buys EVs and car parts. As workers followed the factories, the Korean community has grown to more than 7,000 people. In 2019 a sightseeing boat carrying Korean tourists sank on the Danube in Budapest.
t.know: Budapest was formed in 1873 by merging Buda, Pest and Obuda on both banks of the Danube.
etext: Audi, Mercedes-Benz and Suzuki have long had plants there, and BMW and China's BYD have invested in EV factories. Korean and Chinese battery makers have clustered there, turning it into a European hub for battery production.

Its 9% corporate tax rate is the lowest in the EU, and the government has drawn foreign factories with large subsidies. Close to Germany and with lower labor costs than Western Europe, it serves as a production base for European companies.

Exports lean heavily on the German car industry and foreign-owned plants. It depends heavily on Russian energy, and in early 2023 its inflation was the highest in the EU. Concern about pollution around battery plants is also growing.
